caption_judgement: the caption is substantive, not a restatement of the title: it names both arms (the measured conductor currents and the same row with every shipped poloidal conductor channel scaled by 1.1), states that the level set is shared and inside the vessel, gives the null vocabulary (filled triangle = magnetic axis, filled cross = the arm's own lower X-point, hollow cross = the base arm's), gives the displacement scaling the currents produces (6.7 cm and 1.20 Wb) against the build-time-seam arm (0.0006 cm and 0.00002 Wb), and discloses that both arms are solved on the registered pseudo-wall and neither qualifies a diverted root, so the panel is not evidence of wall closure. No caption finding is recorded.

figure_reviewed.method: judged only the attached rendered PNG; no SVG and no other image was opened, read, listed, searched, rendered or shown; the drawing script and its style module were read for anchoring only

findings.summary: COLUMN_WIDTH = 0.36 gives each panel an axes box 504 px wide on the 14 in canvas, but with set_aspect('equal') over a 1.78 m by 3.28 m domain the plotted content is only about 300 px wide, so roughly 100 px of blank box lies on each side of each panel: on the render the left panel's data span x 185-486, the right panel's x 885-1185, and the two states the figure exists to compare are separated by about 400 px of white, with the pair occupying 42% of the canvas width while the rest is margin. The panel titles (line 124) and the offset captions (line 129) are placed at the axes-box left rather than at the visible data region, so each label hangs about 100 px to the left of the picture it names (title band starts x 85 and x 784; panel borders at x 185 and x 885). It does not stop a reader reading the figure, but the side-by-side comparison is spread across a mostly empty canvas.

The view limits pad the flux grid by 0.04 m in each direction (lines 119-120), but the drawn wall extends 0.034 m past the grid in R and 0.064 m in Z (wall R 0.806-2.574, Z -1.664-1.664 against grid R 0.840-2.540, Z -1.600-1.600), so only the wall's two near-vertical legs fall inside the view and its top and bottom close just outside the ylim and are clipped away. On the render the vessel the caption says is drawn reads as two full-height #929292 vertical rules at the panel borders (x 185 and 486 left, x 885 and 1185 right, spanning y 100-658 with no horizontal segment anywhere), indistinguishable from a plot frame. Because the axis furniture is deliberately off, those two rules are the only machine-geometry reference in the panel, so a reader has no visible scale in R or Z; the flux topology and both null sets remain visible, so this does not hold the node.

item_verdicts.contrast: pass: every element is #3366cc or #333333 on white, at 5.4:1 and 12.6:1; the 1.2 pt contour lines and the wall at 3.1:1 clear the 3:1 graphical threshold, so no mark or label is washed out.
item_verdicts.data_ink: pass: the ink is entirely data (contour strokes, the wall, the null markers) plus four short labels; there is no gradient, fill, band or reference rule, and the strongest weight is the contour set at 1.2 pt with the markers on top. Caveat recorded as a finding: the panels occupy only 42% of the canvas width, so the comparison is spread across a largely empty page.
item_verdicts.decoration: pass: white ground, no gridlines, no background fill, no spines or ticks (axis off), no legend furniture or drop styling.
item_verdicts.label_collision: pass: text bands are disjoint and inside the canvas - titles y 20-35 (x 85-266 and 784-1018), panel ink y 100-658, offset captions y 685-699 (x 85-646 and 784-1352); the whole ink bounding box is x 85-1351 by y 20-699 in 1399x720, at least 21 px clear on every edge, and the guard's clipping/overlap/over-data checks agree with the render. The right panel's two red glyph clusters at x 959-975 sit 12 px apart at their centres (filled cross ends y 570, hollow cross begins y 571), so neither hides the other.
item_verdicts.legibility: pass: two poloidal panels at 300x558 px each carry one blue contour set on 20 shared levels, a filled triangle at the magnetic axis and a filled cross at the lower X-point in both, plus the hollow base-arm cross on the right; the arm name sits above each panel and its offset/residual numbers below, so the lower-null movement (12 px up and 6 px inboard between arms) is readable at a glance. Caveat recorded as a finding: the vessel is visible only as two vertical rules, so there is no printed scale.
item_verdicts.table_form: pass: the image is two spatial flux maps whose reading is the contour topology and the displacement of a null, a spatial relationship the contour set carries at a glance; the exact offsets and residuals are given as short annotations rather than a table standing in for the picture.
